title: Coal miners protest at Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina government headquarters over unpaid wages and pension obligations
location: Sarajevo, in front of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina government building; march from railway station
scope: cross-mine gathering in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina; national scope not established
organizer: Sindikalna organizacija RMU Zenica; colleagues from other Elektroprivreda BiH mines joined
participants_original: Klix: more than 500. RFE/RL: around 150 Zenica miners plus 300–350 colleagues from other Federation mines (approximate).
threshold_50_evidence: Both contemporary reports describe several hundred attendees; Klix states >500 and RFE/RL reports about 150 plus 300–350 colleagues.

start_date.summary: Both articles date the gathering to 21 July 2025.

location.summary: In front of the FBiH government headquarters in Sarajevo, with procession from the railway station.

participants_original.summary: More than 500 reported by Klix; RFE/RL gives approximate components of 150 and 300–350.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both sources report several hundred miners, well above 50.

state_target.summary: Gathering outside the FBiH government headquarters, pressuring authorities and ministry representatives on wage and pension obligations.

organizer.summary: Zenica miners union organized; workers from other FBiH mines joined.

demands.summary: Unpaid wages and pension contributions/retirement obligations, under collective agreement and state-owned mining-sector policy.

state_response.summary: RFE/RL reports ministry representatives agreed to pay May wages by week end and address pension cases by 15 August; some miners remained unconvinced.

protester_violence.summary: No explicit description either way; unknown.

end_date.summary: Some miners said they would remain camped after the agreement announcement; date of closure is not reported.

notes: Do not treat salary agreement announcement as protest closure. Several participants reportedly continued camping; follow up in August. Approximate attendance figures should not be summed into a precise total.
open_questions: Did the camp continue into August, and when did it end?
Did the government implement the promised wage payment and pension steps?
Are there independent reports clarifying attendance and the number who remained?
